summary: House Bill 752, signed by Governor Brad Little and effective 1 July 2026, makes it a crime for a transgender person to use a restroom or changing room that does not match the sex assigned at birth. It reaches government buildings and public-facing private businesses, including gas stations, restaurants, entertainment venues and hospitals. A first offence is a misdemeanour carrying up to one year in jail. The ACLU of Idaho filed suit on 30 April 2026 on due-process, equal-protection and privacy grounds, arguing the law targets no criminal conduct; six transgender Idahoans are plaintiffs in the challenge, brought before the effect date. According to the ACLU, Idaho's is the only state law extending bathroom criminalisation to private businesses, and it carries steeper penalties than other states' bans.
tangentialFactors:
Idaho's bathroom statute is the only state law of its kind reaching private businesses, and the ACLU assesses its penalties as steeper than comparable state bans. The state's continued X option on driver's licences and identity cards diverges from the position on national travel documents, so a visitor may hold a state-issued credential that does not match the marker available on a passport.

A 2022 House-passed bill that would have imposed felony liability and up to life imprisonment on parents who took their children out of state for gender-affirming care was blocked in the Senate. A bill passed by the House in February 2024 and pending in the Senate would recognise only male and female throughout Idaho Code.
localsOnly:
Idaho bars any change of sex on birth certificates, permitting only male or female sex at birth. The 2018 implementation law was allowed into legal effect in January 2026, ending a period from 6 April 2018 when transgender people could change birth certificates to reflect gender identity after a 2017 lawsuit. A 2020 statute, HB 509, that would have reversed that position was ruled moot and unenforceable on 7 August 2020 by District Judge David C. Nye, with $321,000 in attorneys' fees awarded to Lambda Legal and approved in August 2022.

In November 2019 the Board of Health and Welfare removed doctor approval for a gender change for transgender minors, retaining parental permission, emancipation or a court order as the routes.

Transgender prisoners may receive hormone therapy under a September 2024 federal ruling that nullified a 1997 state law banning it.

An April 2024 law bars teachers and education agencies from using pronouns for students that are not based on birth certificates. Transgender athletes are barred from public school and university teams matching their gender identity under legislation signed 30 March 2020. A March 2026 law requires schools, childcare providers and medical professionals to disclose a transgender minor's status to parents within three days of learning it.

County and city ordinances covering gender identity reach about 40% of the population: Ada County, Bellevue, Boise, Coeur d'Alene, Driggs, Hailey, Idaho Falls, Ketchum, Lewiston, Meridian, Moscow, Pocatello, Sandpoint and Victor, plus employee protection in Latah County.
outOfScopeNotes:
Sources differ on the classification of the bathroom offence: the ACLU of Idaho describes a first offence as a misdemeanour carrying up to one year in jail, while one encyclopedia entry describes it as a felony. The discrepancy is unresolved.

Whether the 16 June 2026 narrowing by U.S. District Judge Amanda Brailsford remains in force, and the outcome of the ACLU of Idaho suit, are not established by the sources reviewed.

No record of enforcement action under House Bill 752 against a visitor or resident was identified in the sources reviewed.

No Idaho-specific data on violence against transgender people that is materially above the state's general homicide rate was identified in the sources reviewed.

The current litigation status of the 2018 birth-certificate implementation law is not sourced.
